predictions.experiment: Phenomenon on Math: Math 3.1 cue minus Math 3.0 cue right answers in the longest quartile of MATH-500 by RL (T2) answer length, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, one sample each.
predictions.recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/axis/math500-01/vectors.json (with its manifest.json) and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. Arms: M30 = the arm whose manifest model is allenai/Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math with the cue prompt; M31 = the arm named rl_cue if present, otherwise the first arm in manifest order whose manifest model is allenai/Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math with the cue prompt and no weight edit. Align each arm's 0/1 v3 vector to problem_index through vectors.json problem_indices. Quartiles: sort the 500 problems by t2_generated_tokens ascending, ties broken by problem_index ascending; Q4 = ranks 376-500 (cap hits at their stored token count). A problem missing from an arm counts 0 in that arm; cap hits are whatever 0/1 the vector holds. Statistic: (sum of M31 over Q4) minus (sum of M30 over Q4), a signed integer.
predictions.note: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/axis/math500-01/vectors.json + manifest.json, studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. The manifest has no 'model' field; the model is identified from each arm's 'what' text: M30 = math30_cue ('Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math (3.0), cue', prompt cue), M31 = rl_cue (present, 'RL-Zero-Math 3.1, cue'). Vectors are v3 0/1 aligned through problem_indices; missing counts 0 (none expected, all 500 present). Q4 = ranks 376-500 after sorting by (t2_generated_tokens, problem_index); T2 cap hits sit at their stored count (16,384), so they all fall in Q4. Statistic = sum M31 - sum M30 over Q4; bootstrap over the 125 Q4 problems (pairs). Not a group contrast (same problems, two arms), so no groups line; n = 125. Alt reading: Q4 by value threshold, including every problem tied with the rank-376 length (equals the main number if no tie crosses the boundary). Caveat: T2 is the rl plain sample, a different sampling of 3.1 than the rl_cue arm scored here, as the recipe intends.

predictions.experiment: Where the effect should not appear: Math 3.1 cue minus Math 3.0 cue right answers on the shorter half (Q1+Q2 by T2 length) of MATH-500, T 1.0. A stop-early policy loses nothing on short problems; a uniform-deficit rival spreads the 9-problem overall gap (457 vs 448) over all lengths, about +4 to +5 here.
predictions.recipe: Same files, arms, alignment and missing-row rule as the previous prediction. Q1+Q2 = the 250 problems with the lowest t2_generated_tokens (ties by problem_index ascending; ranks 1-250). Statistic: (sum of M31 over Q1+Q2) minus (sum of M30 over Q1+Q2), a signed integer.
predictions.note: Same files and arm choice as k 1 (math30_cue vs rl_cue, identified via the manifest 'what' text since there is no model field). Short half = ranks 1-250 by (t2_generated_tokens, problem_index). Statistic = sum M31 - sum M30 over those 250; bootstrap over the 250 problems; n = 250. Refuted if measured > 5. Alt reading: short half by value threshold, including every problem tied with the rank-250 length.

predictions.experiment: Mechanism test (length shortening confined to long problems), Math 3.0 first release vs Math 3.1 step 2,800, plain MATH-500, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95: median log ratio of finished lengths in the top T2-length quartile minus the same in the short half. The nearest rival (3.0 is a uniformly less-trained policy, shorter by the same factor everywhere) predicts about 0.00; this mechanism predicts clearly negative.
predictions.recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/fr-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (A, first release = 3.0) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s2800-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (B, 3.1 step 2,800), fetched as in inventory.md, and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. In A and B keep rows with sample == 0, then the first row per problem_index in file order. Paired set S = problem_index values with a kept row in both files and cap_hit false in both. For each problem in S, r = ln(max(n_new_A,1) / max(n_new_B,1)). Quartiles from per_problem.json: sort the 500 problems by t2_generated_tokens ascending, ties by problem_index ascending; Q4 = ranks 376-500, short half = ranks 1-250. L4 = median of r over S problems in Q4; Ls = median of r over S problems in the short half (even count: mean of the two middle values). Statistic = L4 - Ls. No grading is needed. Problems missing from per_problem.json are dropped. If either group has fewer than 20 problems, the statistic counts as refuted.
predictions.note: Files: s3 r3/fr-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (A, 3.0) and r3/s2800-01/out/P_math500.jsonl (B, 3.1 step 2,800), fetched to runs/theory-tests/r3/<run>/out/, plus per_problem.json. Keep sample == 0, first row per problem_index; S = problems kept in both with cap_hit false in both; r = ln(max(n_new_A,1)/max(n_new_B,1)). Q4 = T2 ranks 376-500, short half = ranks 1-250 over all 500 per_problem rows (ranks not recomputed within S). statistics.median gives mean of the two middle values for even counts. Groups line gives the S sizes in Q4 and short half; n = smaller one; fewer than 20 in either -> refuted_without_number. Bootstrap resamples the S problems that lie in Q4 or short half (Q3 problems do not enter the statistic); a resample with an empty group would return 0.0 (practically impossible at these sizes). Alt reading (unpaired): per group ln(median finished n_new of 3.0 / median finished n_new of 3.1), each model's finished rows taken on its own without requiring the other model to finish. Caveat: excluding problems where either model hit the cap removes the longest problems mostly from Q4, which can bias the Q4 median toward problems both finished; the fr-01 run used the 3.1 tokenizer and prompt (known confound).

predictions.experiment: Cause test, the 12k cliff: among finished MATH-500 answers at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 (plain and cue pooled), the ratio of answers of at least 12,000 tokens to answers of 8,000-11,999 tokens, Math 3.0 first release divided by Math 3.1 step 2,800. A uniform-shortening rival gives about 0.8 to 1.0; a 12k training budget gives a clear cliff.
predictions.recipe: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/fr-01/out/P_math500.jsonl and .../fr-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (3.0), s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r3/s2800-01/out/P_math500.jsonl and .../s2800-01/out/F_math500.jsonl (3.1), fetched as in inventory.md. In each of the four files keep rows with sample == 0, then the first row per problem_index in file order. Keep only rows with cap_hit false (cap hits are excluded entirely). Pool each model's P and F kept rows. For each model, A_m = number of pooled rows with 8000 <= n_new < 12000 and B_m = number with n_new >= 12000. R_m = B_m / A_m. Statistic = R(3.0) / R(3.1). If A(3.0), A(3.1) or B(3.1) is 0, the statistic counts as refuted.
predictions.note: Files: s3 r3/fr-01/out/{P,F}_math500.jsonl (3.0) and r3/s2800-01/out/{P,F}_math500.jsonl (3.1), in runs/theory-tests/r3/. Each file: sample == 0, first row per problem_index, then cap_hit false only; P and F pooled per model. A_m = count 8000 <= n_new < 12000, B_m = count n_new >= 12000; statistic (B30/A30)/(B31/A31). If A30, A31 or B31 is 0 -> refuted_without_number. B30 = 0 gives measured 0 (defined, not refuted). Groups line gives the four counts; n = the smallest of the four counts (the tail counts are what the ratio depends on; it can be small). Bootstrap: one entry per problem_index holding that problem's kept finished rows across the four files; a resample where the ratio is undefined returns +inf, so the upper interval end may print as Infinity. Alt reading: the same with n_generated (= n_new + 1 in the rows seen) instead of n_new, which only moves rows sitting exactly at the 8,000 / 12,000 boundaries. example_row has the text and prefill_ids fields removed for size.
